main_text.p: pirici, Methodicique hic vehemen- tér errant. illi enim neglectis caufis, folâ experientiâ & analogismo ad sa- lubria eligenda, & infalubria evitan- da contenti sunt: at hi neglectâ expe- rientiâ, rejectisque caufis, & faculta- tibus, solam indicationem à morbo, & evidentibus communitatibus sum- ptam, ad curationem sufficere arbi- trantur. Dogmatici, & rationales Medici, rationi experientiam adjun- gunt; confiderantq; non tantum cau- sas evidentes, sed & abditas, non neglectis partibus, locis affectis, eo- rumque signis. Ratio enim & expe- rientia se mutuo juvant; pulchrum enim est, judicium rationis ab expe- rientiâ confirmari. proinde dogma- tici his duobus fulcris experientiâ in singularibus, & ratione in universali- bus quasi nixi, multo felicius & ac- curatius curant.
Medendi methodus est ratio inve- niendi certa cuique morbo remedia, sani- tatis gratiâ, per convenientes indicatio- nes. Ratio hæc procedit à communi- bus,

page.notes: Right-hand strip is the edge of the facing page (partly cut, fragmentary marginal words such as "Instru", "bus, & gene", "ad speciales"); not transcribed as text. Heading-like marks are absent. Text of the first line is partly obscured by the binding shadow; readings "pirici" and "sa-" are as far as legible.
